subChunks.title: Writing Tailwind Plugins
subChunks.hookHtml: Tailwind v4's CSS-first approach handles most customisation needs through @theme, @utility, and @variant. But there are scenarios where JavaScript plugins remain the right tool: generating utilities from dynamic scales, adding PostCSS transforms, distributing reusable utility sets as npm packages, or integrating with third-party tools. Writing plugins is the last mile of Tailwind mastery.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
Grand Archmage Solomon: "CSS-first is the right default. A plugin is justified when you need to distribute utilities as a package, generate from a computed scale, or add PostCSS logic. If you can solve it in CSS, solve it in CSS. Reach for a plugin only when CSS cannot express the requirement."

When to use plugins vs CSS-first

  • Use CSS @theme/@utility: custom tokens, static utility variants, project-specific patterns
  • Use plugins: distributable packages, computed scales, PostCSS transforms, third-party integrations

Plugin anatomy in Tailwind v4

// tailwind.config.ts (still supported in v4 alongside CSS config)
import plugin from 'tailwindcss/plugin';

export default {
  plugins: [
    plugin(function({ addBase, addComponents, addUtilities, matchUtilities, theme }) {
      // addBase: CSS in @layer base
      // addComponents: CSS in @layer components
      // addUtilities: CSS in @layer utilities
      // matchUtilities: dynamic value utilities
      // theme(): read design tokens
    })
  ]
};

addBase — base styles and font faces

plugin(function({ addBase }) {
  addBase({
    'html': { 'font-family': 'Inter, sans-serif' },
    ':focus-visible': {
      'outline': '2px solid var(--color-primary)',
      'outline-offset': '2px',
    },
    // Base resets applied to all pages using this plugin
  });
})

addUtilities — static utility classes

plugin(function({ addUtilities }) {
  addUtilities({
    '.text-balance': { 'text-wrap': 'balance' },
    '.text-pretty': { 'text-wrap': 'pretty' },
    '.scrollbar-hidden': {
      '-ms-overflow-style': 'none',
      'scrollbar-width': 'none',
      '&::-webkit-scrollbar': { display: 'none' },
    },
    '.gpu': {
      'transform': 'translateZ(0)',
      'will-change': 'transform',
    },
  });
})

matchUtilities — dynamic value utilities

This is the most powerful plugin API. It generates utilities that accept arbitrary values, just like Tailwind's built-in utilities:

plugin(function({ matchUtilities, theme }) {
  matchUtilities(
    {
      // 'tab-size' becomes the prefix: tab-size-4, tab-size-[8]
      'tab-size': (value) => ({
        'tab-size': value,
      }),
    },
    {
      values: theme('spacing'),  // Use spacing scale as valid values
      supportsNegativeValues: false,
    }
  );
})

addComponents — multi-property component classes

plugin(function({ addComponents, theme }) {
  addComponents({
    '.btn-base': {
      display: 'inline-flex',
      alignItems: 'center',
      justifyContent: 'center',
      fontWeight: theme('fontWeight.medium'),
      borderRadius: theme('borderRadius.md'),
      transitionProperty: theme('transitionProperty.colors'),
      transitionDuration: theme('transitionDuration.150'),
      '&:focus-visible': {
        outline: '2px solid currentColor',
        outlineOffset: '2px',
      },
      '&:disabled': {
        opacity: '0.5',
        cursor: 'not-allowed',
      },
    },
  });
})

Publishing a plugin as an npm package

// packages/tailwind-arcane/src/index.ts
import plugin from 'tailwindcss/plugin';

export default plugin(function({ addUtilities, addBase, matchUtilities }) {
  // Plugin logic here
}, {
  // Default theme extensions
  theme: {
    extend: {
      colors: {
        arcane: { 500: '#6366f1', 600: '#4f46e5' },
      }
    }
  }
});

// apps/web/tailwind.config.ts
import arcanePlugin from '@my-org/tailwind-arcane';
export default { plugins: [arcanePlugin] };

Solomon: "matchUtilities is the most commonly overlooked API. It is what separates a utility that only works at one value from one that works at any value — a meaningful difference for a distributed package."

storyBeats.speaker: Grand Archmage Solomon
storyBeats.text: The plugin API is the bridge between CSS-first configuration and JavaScript logic. Use it when you need to distribute, compute, or transform. The four methods — addBase, addUtilities, addComponents, matchUtilities — each has a specific domain. Learn which to reach for and when.

storyBeats.speaker: matchUtilities — dynamic value utility

subChunks.guidedPracticeHtml:
Build a utility showcase demonstrating plugin-style CSS utilities applied directly to HTML:

  • .plug-card: bg-white, rounded-xl, border, border-gray-200, p-6, shadow-sm
  • .plug-header: flex, items-center, justify-between, mb-4
  • .plug-title: font-semibold, text-gray-900
  • .plug-badge: inline-flex, items-center, gap-1, text-xs, font-medium, px-2, py-0.5, rounded-full, bg-violet-100, text-violet-800
  • .plug-code: font-mono, text-sm, bg-gray-50, rounded-lg, p-4, text-gray-700, border, border-gray-100
  • .plug-list: space-y-2, mt-4
  • .plug-item: flex, items-start, gap-2, text-sm, text-gray-600
subChunks.guidedPracticeStarterCode:
addUtilities

Static
.text-balance { text-wrap: balance; } .scrollbar-hidden { scrollbar-width: none; }
  • ✓ No arbitrary value support
  • ✓ Best for fixed, named utilities

matchUtilities

Dynamic
matchUtilities( { 'tab-size': (v) => ({ 'tab-size': v }) }, { values: theme('spacing') } );
  • ✓ Supports arbitrary values tab-size-[8]
  • ✓ Best for scale-based utilities
subChunks.soloPracticeHtml: Design a plugin API reference card from scratch. It should list all four plugin methods (addBase, addUtilities, addComponents, matchUtilities), show a code example for each, and indicate when to use each method vs the CSS-first alternative. No starter code.
subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain the difference between addUtilities and matchUtilities in a Tailwind plugin. When would you choose matchUtilities? Give an example of a utility that only makes sense with matchUtilities, not addUtilities. Then explain when you would use a CSS-first @utility instead of either plugin method.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between addUtilities and matchUtilities in a Tailwind plugin?
options: addUtilities registers static utility classes; matchUtilities generates utilities that accept arbitrary and theme values (e.g., tab-size-4, tab-size-[8px])
addUtilities adds utilities to @layer utilities; matchUtilities adds them to @layer components
addUtilities is for v3; matchUtilities is the v4 replacement
addUtilities generates one class per call; matchUtilities generates a class for every breakpoint
questions.answer: addUtilities registers static utility classes; matchUtilities generates utilities that accept arbitrary and theme values (e.g., tab-size-4, tab-size-[8px])
questions.explanation: addUtilities takes a fixed object of class-to-CSS mappings — each class name is literal. matchUtilities takes a function that receives a value and returns CSS — Tailwind generates one class per value in the provided scale, plus arbitrary value support. matchUtilities is the right choice when the utility needs to work at multiple scale values, like tab-size-1, tab-size-4, or tab-size-[6px].

questions.prompt: You want to add a universal focus-visible outline style (2px solid currentColor, 2px offset) that applies to all elements across the entire application. Which plugin method is correct?
options: addBase — because focus-visible styles are baseline resets that belong in @layer base
addUtilities — because focus-visible is a utility variant
addComponents — because focus styles are component-level concerns
matchUtilities — because focus-visible needs to accept arbitrary colour values
questions.answer: addBase — because focus-visible styles are baseline resets that belong in @layer base
questions.explanation: addBase injects CSS into @layer base — the correct layer for global resets, defaults, and baseline styles that apply to all elements. Focus-visible resets (removing the default outline and adding a custom one) are base-level concerns, not utility classes. addComponents would be wrong because component classes need a class name to be applied; addBase can target bare element selectors.

questions.prompt: Your team wants to add a .scrollbar-hidden utility (sets scrollbar-width: none and hides ::-webkit-scrollbar). Should this be a CSS @utility in your project's CSS file, or an addUtilities call in a plugin?
options: CSS @utility — it is a project-specific static utility that does not need distribution; CSS-first is the right default for project-local utilities
addUtilities plugin — all utilities must be defined in JavaScript to be properly scanned by the JIT engine
addComponents plugin — utilities with pseudo-element selectors must use the plugin API
Neither — scrollbar styles cannot be added via Tailwind and require a separate CSS file
questions.answer: CSS @utility — it is a project-specific static utility that does not need distribution; CSS-first is the right default for project-local utilities
questions.explanation: In Tailwind v4, @utility in CSS is the preferred way to add project-specific utilities. Plugins add complexity (a JS config file, a dependency) that is only justified when the utilities need to be distributed as a package, access the plugin API for computed scales, or integrate with PostCSS transforms. A simple two-property scrollbar utility is a CSS @utility — clean, fast, and requires no plugin infrastructure.
